'''Narayanan Chandrakumar''' (born 25 November 1951) is an Indian [[chemical physicist]] and a professor of chemistry at the [[Indian Institute of Technology, Madras]].<ref name="Dr. N. Chandrakumar - Faculty profile">{{Cite web |url=http://chem.iitm.ac.in/faculty/chandrakumar/ |title=Dr. N. Chandrakumar - Faculty profile |date=2016 |website=IIT Madras}}</ref> He was the founder of the first [[Nuclear magnetic resonance]] (NMR) laboratory in India and is known for developing a new technique for NMR imaging and diffusion measurement.<ref name="Brief Profile of the Awardee">{{Cite web |url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/Detail.aspx?AID=421 |title=Brief Profile of the Awardee |date=2016 |publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize |access-date=12 November 2016}}</ref> He is an elected fellow of the [[Indian National Science Academy]]<ref name="Indian fellow">{{Cite web |url=http://insaindia.res.in/detail.php?id=N97-1211 |title=Indian fellow |date=2016 |publisher=Indian National Science Academy}}</ref> and the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="Fellow profile">{{Cite web |url=http://www.ias.ac.in/describe/fellow/Chandrakumar,_Prof._Narayanan |title=Fellow profile |date=2016 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences |access-date=12 November 2016}}</ref> The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]], the apex agency of the Government of India for scientific research, awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]], one of the highest Indian science awards, in 1996, for his contributions to chemical sciences.<ref name="View Bhatnagar Awardees">{{cite web | url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/AwardeeList.aspx | title=View Bhatnagar Awardees | publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize | date=2016 | access-date=12 November 2016}}</ref>

== Biography ==
[[File:Loyola College Chennai entrance.jpg|thumb|235px|Loyola College, Chennai]]
N. Chandrakumar, born on 25 November 1951, in the south Indian state of [[Tamil Nadu]], graduated in chemistry from [[Loyola College, Chennai]] in 1970 and completed his master's degree at [[IIT Madras]] in 1972.<ref name="Dr. N. Chandrakumar - Faculty profile" /> His doctoral studies were at [[IIT Kanpur]] under the guidance of [[P. T. Narasimhan]], a [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize|Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar]] laureate, which he completed in 1979 and joined [[Central Leather Research Institute]] (CLRI) as a research associate in 1980. He served the institute till 2001, holding positions such as that of a scientist, head of the Physical Sciences Division and a director-grade scientist and moved to IIT Madras where he is a professor at the department of chemistry. In between, he served as visiting scientist at [[JEOL]], [[National Institutes of Health]] (1986), and at [[University of Siegen]] (1993). He also had visiting professorships at [[University of Ulm]] (1997–98) and [[Inserm|INSERM]], [[Grenoble]] (2001).<ref name="Indian fellow" />

== Legacy ==
Chandrakumar joined as a Scientist in the Chemical Science Lab and set up an 90&nbsp;MHz NMR spectrometer at Central Leather Research Institute. Upon joining IIT Madras, he set up an NMR facility with MRS and MRI to pursue his research at IIT Madras.<ref name="Indian fellow" /> He is the inventor of one of the NMR imaging techniques for diffusion measurements and has done studies on [[Rotating reference frame|rotating frame]] [[Coherence (physics)|coherence]] transfer and multiple [[Magnetic resonance (quantum mechanics)|quantum NMR]], high resolution [[Spin-1/2|spin-1]] NMR and spin-1 connectivity mapping.<ref name="Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners">{{cite web | url=http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf | title=Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners | publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research | date=1999 | access-date=5 October 2016 | pages=34 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304043957/http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf | archive-date=4 March 2016 | url-status=dead }}</ref> He holds seven patents for the processes he has developed.<ref name="Inventions and Patents">{{Cite web |url=http://chem.iitm.ac.in/faculty/chandrakumar/?page_id=361 |title=Inventions and Patents |date=2016 |publisher=IIT Madras}}</ref> His researches have been detailed in two monographs, ''Modern techniques in high-resolution FT-NMR''<ref name="ChandrakumarSubramanian1987">{{cite book|author1=Narayanan Chandrakumar|author2=Sankaran Subramanian|title=Modern techniques in high-resolution FT-NMR|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7KjvAAAAMAAJ|year=1987|publisher=Springer-Verlag|isbn=978-0-387-96327-3}}</ref> and ''Spin-1 NMR''<ref name="Chandrakumar2012">{{cite book|author=N. Chandrakumar|title=Spin-1 NMR|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gVHmCAAAQBAJ|date=6 December 2012|publisher=Springer Science & Business Media|isbn=978-3-642-61089-9}}</ref> and several articles published in peer-reviewed journals.<ref name="Browse by Fellow">{{Cite web |url=http://repository.ias.ac.in/view/fellows/Chandrakumar=3ANarayanan=3A=3A.html |title=Browse by Fellow |date=2016 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences}}</ref> [[ResearchGate]], an online article repository, has listed 85 of them.<ref name="N. Chandrakumar on ResearchGate">{{Cite web |url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/N_Chandrakumar |title=N. Chandrakumar on ResearchGate |date=2016 }}</ref> He has also edited the journals ''Magnetic Resonance, Diamond Jubilee Special Issue of the Proceedings (Chemical Sciences)'' of the Indian Academy of Sciences.<ref name="Books">{{Cite web |url=http://chem.iitm.ac.in/faculty/chandrakumar/?page_id=363 |title=Books |date=2016 |publisher=IIT Madras}}</ref> He has also supervised several doctoral scholars in their studies.<ref name="Indian fellow" />

== Awards and honors ==
Chadrakumar received the [[Bruker]] Young Scientist Award in 1985. Two years later, he received the Young Scientist Award of the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research in its first issue in 1987.<ref name="Indian fellow" /> CSIR honored him again in 1996 with the New Idea Fund Award and the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize]], one of the highest Indian science awards, in 1996.<ref name="Chemical Sciences">{{cite web | url=http://www.csir.res.in/External/Heads/career/award/BPRIZE/CHEMICAL_SCIENCES.htm | title=Chemical Sciences | publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research | date=2016 | access-date=7 November 2016 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120912012851/http://www.csir.res.in/external/heads/career/award/BPRIZE/CHEMICAL_SCIENCES.htm | archive-date=12 September 2012 }}</ref> He was awarded the Millennium Medal by the [[Indian Science Congress Association]] in 2000 and the [[Chemical Research Society of India]] awarded him the Silver Medal in 2008.<ref name="Awards: Year - 2008">{{Cite web |url=http://www.crsi.org.in/index.php/crsi-awards/year-1999-2008 |title=Awards: Year - 2008 |date=2016 |publisher=Chemical Research Society of India |access-date=26 November 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161016123938/http://www.crsi.org.in/index.php/crsi-awards/year-1999-2008 |archive-date=16 October 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref> The award orations he has delivered include Professor R. K. Asundi Memorial Lecture (2002), the Professor [[Kotcherlakota Rangadhama Rao|K. Rangadhama Rao]] Memorial Lecture (2004) of the Indian National Science Academy and the Professor N. Venkatasubramanian Endowment Lecture (2003).<ref name="Awards and honors">{{Cite web |url=http://chem.iitm.ac.in/faculty/chandrakumar/?page_id=72 |title=Awards and honors |date=2016 |publisher=IIT Madras}}</ref> The Indian Academy of Sciences elected him as their fellow in 1993<ref name="Fellow profile" /> and he became a fellow of the Indian National Science Academy in 1997. He also held the INSA-[[German Research Foundation|DFG]] Exchange Fellowship in 1988, Fellowship of the [[Max Planck Society|Max Planck Gesellschaft]] in 1989 and, 1990, INSA Visiting Fellowship for MRI / MRS Research at [[All India Institutes of Medical Sciences|AIIMS]] in 1994, Honorary Senior Fellowship of the [[Jawaharlal Nehru Center for Advanced Scientific Research]] in 1997 and the [[Jagadish Chandra Bose|J. C. Bose]] National Fellowship in 2009.<ref name="Indian fellow" />
